thread:
anna_support: Raising an escalation from Acme Corp — their Private deployment started failing for streaming inference. They see intermittent TLS handshake errors and streaming connections drop after ~10s. Customer logs: 

customer_acct: Logs from our side: 
- client: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"
- model proxy: "TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure"
- app: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" (only sometimes)

anna_support: They say non-streaming requests (single-shot) usually work, but long poll/stream sessions are flaky. Asking infra/network for packet-level help. @liam_infra @rachel_network can you triage?

liam_infra: Can you capture a tcpdump from the customer edge or the private router? Start with: 
```
sudo tcpdump -nni any host 198.51.100.23 and port 443 -w /tmp/stream-fail.pcap
```
Also ask them to run an `openssl s_client` to check cert chain and SNI: 
```
openssl s_client -connect model.acme-internal.example.com:443 -servername model.acme.example.com -alpn h2
```

customer_acct: Pcap attached (shared to support drive). Ran openssl — sometimes chain shows a local gateway CA, sometimes real cert. We use a FortiGate for outbound DPI/SSL inspection.

rachel_network: FortiGate + SSL inspection explains the x509. For the streaming drops, check for RSTs and asymmetric routing. I pulled the pcap — here's the relevant slice: 
```
15:11:02.123 IP 10.10.5.12.52345 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
15:11:02.203 IP 198.51.100.23.443 > 10.10.5.12.52345: Flags [S.], seq 54321, ack 12346, length 0
15:11:02.204 IP 10.10.5.12.52345 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [.], ack 54322, length 0
15:11:12.210 IP 198.51.100.23.443 > 10.10.5.12.52345: Flags [RST], seq 54322, length 0  <-- RST from remote (Fortigate IP 198.51.100.23)
```

rachel_network: The RST originates from the upstream edge 198.51.100.23 (their FortiGate). That matches a DPI policy closing long-lived streams when it detects non-standard or idle patterns. Also saw cases where the gateway terminates TLS and reissues cert signed by its local CA — hence x509 complaints when the client doesn't trust that CA.

liam_infra: Two likely fixes: 
- If they want MITM/inspection off for Redwood endpoints: add an allowlist rule on FortiGate for `model.acme-internal.example.com` (SNI) or the specific destination IPs to bypass SSL inspection. 
- Alternatively, deploy the FortiGate CA into client trusts so TLS re-signing doesn't break auth. But for streaming we prefer bypass because DPI may buffer and cut the stream.

customer_acct: We can add an allowlist but need exact hostnames/IPs. Do you have the Redwood egress IPs for Private?

anna_support: For Private deployments we publish the control/ingress IP set per-customer. I've pasted the current egress CIDR used by Acme's Private stack: `198.51.100.0/26` and the model hostnames they call out: `model.acme-internal.example.com` and `s3-backup.acme-internal.example.com` (for caching). Confirm before they change firewall rules.

rachel_network: Also note NACLs and stateful SGs: make sure ephemeral ports (1024-65535) are allowed on return path. If FortiGate inspects and terminates TLS, it will open new TCP flows to the model cluster — SAs must allow those. For AWS NACLs we recommend allowing ephemeral range 1024-65535 for both inbound/outbound if you're NATting.

liam_infra: Quick repro test customers can run: 
```
# check if gateway is replacing cert
openssl s_client -connect model.acme-internal.example.com:443 -servername model.acme.example.com | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -subject
```
If issuer is FortiGate CA, then SSL inspection is active.

customer_acct: Ran that — issuer is `Fortinet NSS CA`. So inspection enabled. We disabled SSL inspection for the hostname and re-ran a stream — streaming stayed up for 12+ minutes with no resets.

anna_support: Great confirmation. Next steps: 
- Customer to add allowlist SNI/IP on FortiGate for our Private egress ranges (198.51.100.0/26).
- Ensure NACL allows ephemeral return ports if using NAT.
- If they cannot bypass, install Forti CA into all clients (not ideal for security).

customer_acct: We'll update firewall rules and monitor. Thanks all, @rachel_network @liam_infra :thumbsup:

trace-bot: Incident tagged: #support-1800001234 -> Escalation: firewall SSL inspection causing TLS re-sign and RSTs on streaming. Owner: anna_support.

anna_support: Closing once customer confirms 24h stable. Leaving notes in the ticket about allowinglist and NACL ephemeral port guidance.

customer_acct: Confirmed stable after firewall changes. Closing from our side. Thanks everyone! :white_check_mark:
